@dgpaci thanks, the bug list holds: all six are confirmed in `dynamicform.py` / `dynamicform.js` on develop.

Before splitting this up: how urgent is it for you, and which of the bugs is actually blocking a project right now?

On the redesign part (one storage place for widget attributes, migrating the existing `df_fields`, a new layout), I would rather not invest there. For complex cases the recommended pattern is grouplets, not dynamic fields. A dynamic-field form that needs a `dbSelect` with a `condition` is already a sign the case belongs in a grouplet.

So the proposal is:
- fix the six bugs in one small PR, touching only `dynamicform.py` and `dynamicform.js`, with no change to stored data;
- leave the storage redesign and migration out, and move the complex cases to grouplets.

If one of those cases is urgent for you, tell me which one and we can look at the grouplet version together.

This needs a workflow because the three requested capabilities share one lifecycle contract. The phases are: (1) define terminal-resource placement, precedence with `summary_template`, `startStep` addressing, and new-record reload identity; (2) add the terminal resource by reusing the existing grouplet loader and exclude it from the step menu; (3) centralize initial navigation so reloads of the same document preserve state, including the first insert; (4) cover template/resource, index/code, new/existing records, same-record reload, and record changes in the real booking flow. The existing fix only covers reloads when no summary is present.

A new PR on develop replaces this one; it carries over the shared EndpointPermission check (with the ep_table tag fix), the shared doc popup and the light info icon.

Answering [the review](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/pull/1736#pullrequestreview-5615842361) in 7420059. Thanks for the careful read. All four blocking points held against the code; the push answers each of them, and the minor ones too, except the atomic 409 (below).

> **Any logged user can grant themselves the documenter tags.**

`doc_editor_tags` is gone, together with the page-store write in `gnrwebpage.py`: writing always needs `_DOC_,doc_<pkg>` of the doc's package, resolved server side (`ep_doc.documenterTags(address)`). Only the demo page used it; it now needs a real documenter. Removed test: `test_a_page_may_redefine_the_documenter_tags`.

> **Stored XSS through the front-matter `title`.**

The doc's own title is now treated as text on the client: `genro.dlg._docTitleHtml` escapes it before it reaches the popup or the editor dialog title; a caller's title (a label, a card title) is the caller's markup and stays as it is. New test: `doc_popup.test.js` › "the doc's own title is text…" (fails with the escape removed).

> **Docs are public in the default setup.**

Worse than that: `/_storage/<name>/...` and `/<name>:...` serve *any* storage with no authentication (`storageDispatcher`), so a configured `inlinedoc` S3 service was public too. Now:
- `BaseStorageHandler.isPrivateStorage()`: `inlinedoc` is private by name (`PRIVATE_STORAGES`), any other storage by `private="true"`; `storageDispatcher` answers 404 for a private storage, and the `private` parameter never reaches a service's constructor.
- An unconfigured private storage falls back to a folder of the **instance** (`<instance>/inlinedoc`), not of `site_static_dir`; `DocumentationStore.root` is always `inlinedoc:`.
- New test: `test_no_url_serves_the_docs` (both url forms 404, while a `home` file is still served 200; fails with the check removed).

> **No switch.**

The whole feature is behind `<experimental><gui inlinedoc="true"/></experimental>` (`page.inlineDoc`, passed to the client as `startArgs.inlineDoc`). With the flag off everything is as on `develop`: helper.xml is back (`getHelperData`, `saveHelperValue`, `setHelperData`, `sys/helpeditor`, the developer prompt editor, the "Open helper editor" menu lines), fields carry `helpcode`/`helpcode_package`, grouplet cards keep their inline / `file:` HTML doc, no `_index` request is sent, and `sys/ep_doc` answers 404. With the flag on, a legacy `file:` doc of a card falls back to the resource's own address.

**Minor**
- `_listings` is no longer module state: the listings live on the site (`site.doc_listings`, keyed by domain). The cross-worker staleness you describe now affects only the index (the ⓘ states, 30s): reading a single doc lists its own folder directly, so a doc just written by another worker is read at once and a save based on it does not get a false 409. Test: `test_a_doc_another_process_wrote_is_read_at_once`.
- Uploads: at most 5 MB (`ASSET_MAX_SIZE`, checked before decoding), strict base64, and the bytes must be the declared image (png/jpeg/gif/webp magic numbers).
- `_calling_page_id` as a bearer token: `checkEndpointPermission(same_connection=True)` refuses a request whose connection is not the page's own; `ep_doc` uses it on every call, `ep_table` is unchanged. Test: a page id used from another connection is refused.
- The 409 is still read-then-write: opened as #1745 rather than solved here, since the local storage has no compare-and-swap, and S3 would need conditional writes.

Checks: flake8 clean on the touched files; gnrpy pytest 3335 passed, 21 skipped (tests/sql included); JS 563 passed. Not verified in a browser (neither flag position), and not over real HTTP or S3: the dispatcher is exercised by calling `storageDispatcher` directly.

Thanks, every point held against the code. Answered in four commits on top of `feature/doc-storage`, merged in (fda4ef3), not rebased:

> The way the manual's content reaches the page, though, needs work, and the #1736 points carry over.

([review](https://github.com/genropy/genropy/pull/1738#pullrequestreview-5616445165))

**Security**

1. **XSS from the section title**: the panel's title now goes through `_docTitleHtml`, like the doc's own title in #1736; the manual's title and the doc's title are escaped text, only a caller's `kw.title` stays markup (fda4ef3, tested in a27e4e5).
2. **Deny list**: replaced by an allow list (04403d1). A section keeps the tags a Sphinx section uses, and per tag only the attributes it needs (`href` on `a`, `src`/`alt`/`width`/`height` on `img`, `colspan`/`rowspan`, ...). `svg`, `math`, `base`, `meta`, `link`, forms and embedded content are dropped with what they hold, any other unknown tag keeps only its text, comments go. `style`, `class` and `id` go too, so the manual cannot reach the page's own classes or ids. `href`/`src` are made absolute and kept only when http(s) or a path of the site. Each of your cases is a test row in `test_a_section_keeps_only_the_allow_list`.
3. **`manual.url`**: an inventory entry is used only when its url stays under the folder of the site's `objects.inv`, on the same scheme and host, so `javascript:`, another host, a link-local address or a file outside the site are ignored and never reach the page (04403d1). The panel also checks it again: the link and `openWindow` take only an http(s) url or a path of the site (a27e4e5).
4. **SSRF**: the server reads only the configured pages (an http(s) url or an absolute path) and urls under their site's folder; remote reads follow no redirect, connect within 3 seconds and stop at 2 MB (04403d1). Tested with a real local server answering a 302 to `169.254.169.254` and a page past the size cap.

**Other**

5. **`_cache`**: gone. The cache is the site's (`site.manual_cache`, next to `doc_listings`), bounded to 16 MB with the least recently read out first, and a failure is kept 30 seconds instead of 300 (04403d1). It stays per process, like every cache of the site.
6. **Cold cache, unreachable host**: the first network error stops the walk up the folders and marks the host as down for 30 seconds, so a page's index waits at most one 3-second connect timeout, and other pages on the same host are not asked (04403d1).
7. **Another group's `--variant`**: never shown any more. The user's own pages first, then the label without variant, then nothing (04403d1, `test_the_variant_of_another_groups_manual_is_never_shown`).
8. **Esc**: the panel's listener stops the event, so the form or dialog below does not close with it; inside a dialog above the page (the note's editor among them) Esc stays the dialog's (a27e4e5).
9. **No switch**: `pageHelp`, `vhelp`, `form_help` and the rounded groups' help are built only under `<experimental><gui inlinedoc="true"/>` (0c0df44); without it no help button exists and no page asks `sys/ep_doc` for its index, which already answers 404 since #1736.
10. **Tests skipped in CI**: `gnrmanual_test.py` now reads a manual written in the shape Sphinx publishes it (`objects.inv` and the html of its pages, copied from a real build), so it runs in CI without Sphinx: 34 tests. The one test that builds the manual with Sphinx and myst-parser is skipped where they are not installed (04403d1).

**The #1736 points**

- `doc_editor_tags`: removed with the merge of #1736's fix; Edit and Add a note in the panel go through the same server-side documenter tags.
- `innerHTML` for titles and content: points 1-3 above.
- `home:inlinedoc` served publicly: unchanged here, as you said.
- No switch: point 9.

**Checks**: flake8 (CI selection) clean, full Python suite 3373 passed / 21 skipped, JS suite 566 passed.

Not verified: no browser pass on a running instance; the panel's behaviour (Esc, link, title) is covered by the JS tests only.

A node built inside a detached `GnrDomSource` never subscribes, before or after this change. Subscriptions are added only by `_setDynAttributes`, reached only from `build()` (directly, or via `stripData` -> `moveData`), and `build()` runs only from `_trigger_ins`/`_trigger_upd`, which fire from the `sourceTriggers` subscription that exists on `_main` alone (genro_src.js:129). `newRoot()` returns a bare `GnrDomSource` with no such subscription, and `_trigger_ins` already skips lost nodes (line 221, on develop too).

A detached root is a structure buffer, not a live tree, and that stays as it is.

Thanks — both points addressed in 256fa445ca.

**1. A widget rebuilt over data that stays.** For the ValidationTextBox family (textbox, number/date/time boxes, filteringSelect, dbSelect) the new widget does validate its value when built: `_doBuildNode` (`gnrdomsource.js:1125-1131`), once `genro.src._started`, runs `validationsOnChange(..., validateOnly=true)` and `updateValidationStatus()`, which calls `form.updateInvalidField` for the new node. The new test *a widget rebuilt over a value still invalid makes the form invalid again* pins it: required field empty, old widget torn down (form valid), widget rebuilt → form invalid again, with the entry keyed on the new node only. It uses the real `validatemixin_validationsOnChange` and `GnrValidator`, and fails if that build-time block is disabled.

A bad number is not at stake: the invalid text lives in the old widget only, the data keeps the last valid value, and the rebuilt widget shows that.

What the build-time check does **not** cover is a widget carrying `validate_*` outside the ValidationTextBox family (checkbox, simpleTextArea, ComboBox): rebuilt over an empty required value it reads valid until touched or until the next record load. Before this PR that case stayed invalid only by accident — the stale entry pointed at the lost node, so filling the field on the rebuilt widget never cleared it and the form stayed invalid until the next load. Widening the condition at `gnrdomsource.js:1125` to any node with validations would close it; it changes build-time behaviour for those widgets, so I would keep it out of this PR and open an issue for it, if you agree.

**2. `kw.where`.** Done: `triggerDEL` takes the parent path from `kw.where`; both `del` emitters in `gnrbag.js` (`_pop`, `clear`) pass it.

@genro both points taken, in two commits. The push dismissed your approval and @cgabriel's, and nothing either of you approved has changed shape — this only adds teardown that was missing and removes a function nobody calls.

> **The frozen path still skips the other half of the teardown.** `_trigger_upd` also runs `updatingNode._onDeleting()`, destroys `externalWidget`, and calls `_onDeletingContent(kw.oldvalue)`; `_trigger_del` destroys the widget and the DOM content. None of that happens while the node is frozen, and after `unfreeze()` the rebuild no longer has `kw.oldvalue`, so the discarded widgets are never destroyed.

https://github.com/genropy/genropy/pull/1301#pullrequestreview-5196496164

The hole is there, and I traced it one step further before closing it, because the two halves of it behave differently.

**The dijit widgets are not the leak.** `rebuild()` is `setValue(this._value)` (`gnrdomsource.js:957`), so the unfreeze re-enters `_trigger_upd`, which calls `widgetDestroyAndUnlink(kw.node.widget)` → `destroyRecursive()` on the frozen node's own widget (`genro_src.js:246-288`). The discarded content's widgets are its descendants, so they do go down there.

**What is really never done** is the part no rebuild can reach: the `_onDeleting()` hook chain on the discarded nodes — at unfreeze `_onDeletingContent` runs on the *new* value, never on the one that was thrown away — and the `externalWidget`s, which hang off no dijit parent, so no `destroyRecursive` finds them. Those two now happen where the content is discarded.

**The two events are not symmetric, and this is where I did not follow your comment literally.** On `del` the node is gone for good, so it takes the whole thing: its own `_onDeleting()`, the hooks on its content, its children's `externalWidget`s and its own. On `upd` only the *discarded content* does. Running `updatingNode._onDeleting()` and destroying `updatingNode.externalWidget` there would be wrong: that node is not dying, it is frozen and rebuilds on unfreeze, and tearing it down under freeze takes it off screen before that happens. So the `upd` branch is `_onDeletingContent(kw.oldvalue)` + the externalWidgets under `oldvalue`, behind the same `oldvalue !== _value` guard the subscription cleanup already used.

`deleteChildrenExternalWidget` keeps its signature and delegates to a `deleteContentExternalWidget` taking the content, which is what the `upd` branch has in hand.

**Three cases added to the test file**, and the two that pin new behaviour are real:

```
✖ content replaced under freeze is torn down, the frozen node is not
✖ a node popped under a frozen ancestor is torn down with its content
```

Both fail against the previous frozen branch and pass now. The third — a same-bag rebuild under freeze tears nothing down — passes both ways by design: it guards the `oldvalue !== _value` path against a future regression rather than pinning a change. `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js`: 39/39.

> **`refreshSourceIndexAndSubscribers` is dead code, and has been since #1152.** Zero callers

Right, and gone. One correction: it was not quite zero references. `projects/gnrcore/packages/test/resources/heavy_profiler.js:75` named it in the list of methods it instruments — `wrap` only `console.warn`s on a missing method, so nothing broke, but the entry had to go with the function.

One thing I left standing rather than deciding for you: `_deletingNodeContent` is now written in two places and read nowhere, since that function was its only reader. Removing its reader is this change; removing the counter is a separate call, so I left it.

Still not verified from here: no browser pass on a real batch. The four cases in the test file drive the trigger path in a `vm` with no DOM, so the widget teardown is asserted through spies, not observed.

Follow-up on the point I had left open: `_deletingNodeContent` is gone too, in `00de6092`.

It existed only for the guard at the top of `refreshSourceIndexAndSubscribers`, which stopped the global sweep from restarting while `deleteNodeContent` was emptying a node. With that function removed the counter was written in two places and read in none, which is the same half-finished state your comment objected to in the function itself — so leaving the decision open was the wrong call.

A plain commit on top, not an amend: the branch is pushed and under review, so no history is rewritten. `node --test gnrjs/tests/*.test.js` still 39/39.

Both blocking points and the three notes are addressed in ef0920a95, on top of a rebase on current `develop`. Every finding is now a test that fails on the previous head — I ran them against it before fixing, and the failures reproduce your observations verbatim, including the re-rooting under `site_static_dir` and the two `RecursionError`.

**1. Loop in the parent chain.** `_loopingParentChain` walks the chain on the stored parameters before the parent gets built, and returns `None` on a loop, so the service falls into `UnconfiguredService`. The walk starts from the parent name rather than from the service itself on purpose: `service_name` is assigned only after the factory returns (`services/__init__.py:105`), so at `__init__` time the service does not know its own name — but revisiting any name in the chain is enough to catch both a self-parent and two services pointing at each other. `test_relative_storage_looping_parent_services` and `test_relative_storage_parent_of_itself` cover them; both raised `RecursionError` before.

**2. Missing parent.** The parent is now looked up with `getStorageParameters` first, and an absent one leaves the service unconfigured, so the legacy `site_static_dir` fallback is never reached. `test_relative_storage_missing_parent_service_name` asserts the base path is `None` and that no folder appeared under the site static dir; on the previous head it resolved to `.../site/rel_gone_parent_storage/docs`. `test_relative_storage_deleted_parent_service` reproduces your live scenario — a working relative service, its parent removed, the child re-resolved — and it moved to `.../site/rel_deleted_parent/sub` before, base path `None` now.

**3. Local parent with an empty base path.** Fixed, but at resolution time rather than in the property: a parent whose `base_path` is `None` is refused, so the service is unconfigured instead of exposing a `None` base path that `internal_path` would turn into `os.path.join(None, ...)`. That keeps the `not parent_base_path` branch correct for the bucket-root `''` of s3 and sftp — `BaseLocalService` is the only implementation that yields `None` (`storage.py:737`; sftp and s3 both normalise to `''`). The same check ends the chain on a relative parent that is unconfigured itself, which had the same effect: `test_relative_storage_parent_without_base_path` resolved to `docs` before, `test_relative_storage_on_unconfigured_relative_parent` to `2026` — both relative to the process CWD, as you said.

**4. `UnconfiguredService` refusing less than its docstring.** `delete` now raises, and so do `renameNode` and `duplicateNode`, so every write entry point either raises the message or is unreachable. `size`, `mtime` and `md5hash` I left returning `None`, consistent with `exists()` being false — they are the abstract stubs of `StorageService`, and an empty storage answering "nothing there" reads better than an exception on a read. On `serve`: the base implementation already returns `not_found_exception` when `internal_path` is falsy (`storage.py:665-668`), and `not_found_exception` reads the environ through `Request(environ).url` (`gnrwsgisite.py:1506`), so the `KeyError: 'REQUEST_METHOD'` comes from the synthetic environ rather than from the service — with a real request it is a 404, which is what an empty storage should answer.

**5. Log line without the service name.** It now logs the relative path, as you suggested.

Thanks for the thorough read. All four major points and the six medium ones are addressed in commit `665757574`. Recap below.

### Major points

1. **Scope creep** — turns out the diff was already clean: the PR is exactly one feature commit on top of `develop`, and `c25780309` (gnrwebstruct characterization tests) is *in develop*, not in the PR diff. The branch was just a couple of commits behind upstream `develop`, which made `git log` confusing. Merged `develop` in (commit `9e2b90f9e`) so the log reads cleanly now.

2. **Docs placement** — `docs/groupletgrid_architecture.md` and `docs/groupletgrid_store_integration.html` removed from the repo. > I get the following try to use the test_heavy_build demonstrator: `AttributeError: 'GnrCustomWebPage' object has no attribute 'response'`

Confirmed and fixed. `onIniting` also runs on the websocket registration path (`gnrasync.registerPage → gnrsimplepage.__init__`), where `self.response` does not exist — it is only set in `GnrWebPage.__init__` on the WSGI path. > Having the data storm working (blazing fast!), the rebuild fails

Root cause understood, and it is pre-existing behavior this branch does not touch: `node.rebuild()` is `setValue(this._value)`, i.e. it re-expands the already-expanded source. Component nodes do not survive that — `_beforeCreation` moves their attributes into `_saved_attributes` on first expansion and nothing ever restores them, so the second expansion finds the framepane without its `frameCode` (your exact stack: `createContent` via `walk`). The demo button was asking the framework for an operation it has never supported over expanded components (bagGrid, formbuilder). The button now rebuilds the bound-divs subtree (3000 nodes with dynamic bindings, no components), which is the part that actually demonstrates the incremental subscriber cleanup; the limit is documented in the page docstring. Making components survive a source rebuild (restoring `_saved_attributes` and the original children) is real design work — if you think it is worth it, I would open a dedicated issue rather than widen this PR.
